questions.question: Let ${x}^{k} + {y}^{k} = {a}^{k},\left(a,k > 0\right)$ and $\frac{dy}{dx} + {\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}^{\frac{1}{3}} = 0,$ then $k$ is
questions.explanation: Differentiating the given equation with respect to $x k.{x}^{k - 1} + k.{y}^{k - 1}\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = - {\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)}^{k - 1} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} + {\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)}^{k - 1} = 0 \implies k - 1 = - \frac{1}{3} \implies k = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$

questions.question: Let, $f : R \to R$ be a function such that $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + {x}^{2}f'\left(1\right) + xf''\left(2\right) + f'''\left(3\right),∀x \in R.$ Then $f\left(2\right)$ equals
questions.explanation:
Let, $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + a{x}^{2} + bx + c \implies f'\left(x\right) = 3{x}^{2} + 2ax + b \implies f''\left(x\right) = 6x + 2a \implies f'''\left(x\right) = 6$

According to the question,

$a = f'\left(1\right) = 3 + 2a + b \implies a + b = - 3...\left(i\right) b = f''\left(2\right) = 12 + 2a \implies 2a - b = - 12...\left(ii\right) c = f'''\left(3\right) \implies c = 6$

Solving equations $\left(i\right) & \left(ii\right)$, we get, $a = - 5 & b = 2 \implies f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} - 5{x}^{2} + 2x + 6 ∴f\left(2\right) = 8 - 20 + 4 + 6 = - 2.$

.

questions.question: If $y = y(x)$ is an implicit function of $x$ such that ${\log }_{e}(x + y) = 4xy$, then $\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ at $x = 0$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given:

${\log }_{e}(x + y) = 4xy$

When $x = 0$, then $y = 1 {\log }_{e}\left(x + y\right) = 4xy \implies x + y = {e}^{4xy}$

Now differentiate w.r.t. $x 1 + {y}^{'} = {e}^{4xy}\left(4y + 4x{y}^{'}\right) \dots \left(i\right)$

At $(0,1) \implies {y}^{'}(0) + 1 = 4 \implies {y}^{'}(0) = 3$

Now, again differentiate equation $(i)$, we get

${y}^{"} = {e}^{4xy}{\left(4y + 4x{y}^{′}\right)}^{2} + {e}^{4xy}\left(4{y}^{'} + 4{y}^{'} + 4x{y}^{"}\right)$

At $\left(0,1\right) {y}^{"}(0) = 1(4 \times 1 + 0{)}^{2} + 1(4 \times 3 + 4 \times 3 + 0) \implies {y}^{"}(0) = 16 + 24 = 40 \implies {y}^{"}(0) = 40$

questions.question:
Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $(\sin x \cos y)(f(2 x+2 y)-f(2 x-2 y))=(\cos x \sin \mathrm{y})(f(2 \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y})+f(2 \mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{y}))$, for all $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \in \mathbf{R}$.

If $f^{\prime}(0)=\frac{1}{2}$, then the value of $24 f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)$ is:
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & (\sin x \cos y)(f(2 x+2 y)-f(2 x-2 y))=(\cos x \sin y) \\ & (f(2 x+2 y)+f(2 x-2 y)) \\ & f(2 x+2 y)(\sin (x-y))=f(2 x-2 y) \sin (x+y) \\ & \frac{f(2 x+2 y)}{\sin (x+y)}=\frac{f(2 x-2 y)}{\sin (x-y)} \\ & \text { Put } 2 x+2 y=m, 2 x-2 y=n \\ & \frac{f(m)}{\sin \left(\frac{m}{2}\right)}=\frac{f(n)}{\sin \left(\frac{n}{2}\right)}=\mathrm{K} \\ & \Rightarrow f(m)=K \sin \left(\frac{m}{2}\right) \\ & \therefore f(x)=K \sin \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{K}{2} \cos \left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \\ & P_{\text {Put }} x=0 ; \frac{1}{2}=\frac{K}{2} \Rightarrow K=1 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{4} \sin \frac{x}{2} \\ & 4 f^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)=\left(-\frac{1}{4} \sin \left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)\right) 24 \\ & =\frac{-24}{8}=-3\end{aligned}$

questions.question: Let $f(x)=a x^3+b x^2+c x+41$ be such that $f(1)=40, f^{\prime}(1)=2$ and $f^{\prime}(1)=4$. Then $\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+\mathrm{c}^2$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=a x^3+b x^2+c x+41 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=3 a x^2+2 b x+c x \\ & \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(1)=3 a+2 b+c=2 \ldots(1)\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{n})=6 \mathrm{ax}+2 \mathrm{~b} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(1)=6 \mathrm{a}+2 \mathrm{~b}=4 \\ & 3 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=2 \ldots \ldots \ldots .(2)\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & (1)-(2) \\ & b+c=0...(3)\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}(1)=40 \\ & \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}+41=40 \end{aligned}$ use (3) $a+41=40$ by (2) $\begin{aligned} & -3+b=2 \Rightarrow b=5 \& c=-5 \\ & a^2+b^2+c^2=1+25+25=51 \end{aligned}$

questions.question: Let $f(x) = {x}^{3} + {x}^{2}{f}^{'}(1) + x{f}^{"}(2) + {f}^{'''}(3),x \in R$. Then ${f}^{'}(10)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given: $f(x) = {x}^{3} + {x}^{2}{f}^{'}(1) + x{f}^{"}(2) + {f}^{'''}(3) \implies {f}^{'}(x) = 3{x}^{2} + 2x{f}^{'}(1) + {f}^{"}(2)...\left(i\right) \implies {f}^{"}(x) = 6x + 2{f}^{'}(1)...\left(ii\right) \implies {f}^{'''}(x) = 6 \implies {f}^{'''}(3) = 6...\left(iii\right)$

Using $\left(ii\right)$,

$\implies {f}^{"}(2) = 12 + 2{f}^{'}(1)$

Putting this value in equation $\left(i\right)$,

$\implies {f}^{'}(1) = 3 + 2{f}^{'}(1) + 12 + 2{f}^{'}(1) \implies 0 = 15 + 3{f}^{'}(1) \implies {f}^{'}(1) = - 5...\left(iv\right) \implies {f}^{"}(2) = 12 + 2\left( - 5\right) \implies {f}^{"}(2) = 2...\left(v\right) \implies f(x) = {x}^{3} + {x}^{2} \cdot ( - 5) + x \cdot (2) + 6 \implies {f}^{'}(x) = 3{x}^{2} - 10x + 2 \implies {f}^{'}(10) = 300 - 100 + 2 \implies {f}^{'}(10) = 202$

questions.question: Let $x\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\cos t\sqrt{\sin 2t}$ and $y\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\sin t\sqrt{\sin 2t},t \in \left(0,\frac{\pi }{2}\right)$. Then $\frac{1 + {\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\frac{{d}^{2}y}{{\mathrm{dx}}^{2}}}$ at $t = \frac{\pi }{4}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given

$x = 2\sqrt{2}\cos t\sqrt{\sin 2t}$

Now differentiating w.r.t $t$ both side we get,

$\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{2\sqrt{2}\cos 3t}{\sqrt{\sin 2t}}......\left(1\right)$

Also given $y\left(t\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\sin t\sqrt{\sin 2t}$

Again differentiating w.r.t $t$ both side we get,

$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{2\sqrt{2}\sin 3t}{\sqrt{\sin 2t}}......\left(2\right)$

Now dividing equation $\left(2\right)$ from $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\frac{dy}{dx} = \tan 3t$

Now finding the value of $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $t = \frac{\pi }{4}$ we get,

$\frac{dy}{dx} = - 1$

Now finding $\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ we get,

$\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\frac{{\sec }^{2}3t \cdot \sqrt{\sin 2t}}{\cos 3t}$

Now finding value of $\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ at $t = \frac{\pi }{4}$ we get,

$\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = - 3$

Now putting the value of $\frac{dy}{dx} & \frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ in$\frac{1 + {\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}}$ we get,

$\frac{1 + {\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}^{2}}{\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}} = \frac{1 + 1}{ - 3} = - \frac{2}{3}$

questions.question: If $x = 2\sin \theta - \sin 2\theta$ and $y = 2\cos \theta - \cos 2\theta , \theta \in \left(0,2\pi \right),$ then $\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ at $\theta = \pi$ is:
questions.explanation:
$\frac{dx}{d\theta } = 2\cos \theta - 2\cos 2\theta \frac{dy}{d\theta } = - 2\sin \theta + 2\sin 2\theta ∴\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\sin 2\theta - \sin \theta }{\cos \theta - \cos 2\theta } = \frac{2\sin \frac{\theta }{2}.\cos \frac{3\theta }{2}}{2\sin \frac{\theta }{2}.\sin \frac{3\theta }{2}} = \cot \frac{3\theta }{2} \frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = \frac{d}{d\theta }\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\frac{d\theta }{dx} = - \frac{3}{2}{\mathrm{cosec}}^{2}\frac{3\theta }{2}.\frac{d\theta }{dx} \implies \frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = \frac{ - \frac{3}{2}{\mathrm{cosec}}^{2}\frac{3\theta }{2}}{2\left(\cos \theta - \cos 2\theta \right)} \implies {\left(\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}\right)}_{\theta = \pi } = \frac{3}{4\left( - 1 - 1\right)} = \frac{3}{8}$

:

questions.question: For $x > 1$, if ${\left(2x\right)}^{2y} = 4{e}^{2x - 2y}$, then ${\left(1 + {\log }_{e}⁡2x\right)}^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given, ${\left(2x\right)}^{2y} = 4.{e}^{2x - 2y}$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$2y\text{ }lo{g}_{e}2x = \text{ }lo{g}_{e}4 + \left(2x - 2y\right) \implies 2y = \left(\frac{lo{g}_{e}4 + 2x}{1 + lo{g}_{e}2x}\right)$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get

$\frac{2dy}{dx} = \frac{\left(1 + {\log }_{e}2x\right).2 - \left({\log }_{e}4 + 2x\right)\frac{1}{x}}{{\left(1 + {\log }_{e}2x\right)}^{2}}$ (Using quotient rule)

$\implies {\left(1 + {\log }_{e}2x\right)}^{2}\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(\frac{x.lo{g}_{e}2x - lo{g}_{e}2}{x}\right)$.

questions.question: If $y\left(x\right) = {x}^{x},x > 0$, then ${y}^{"}\left(2\right) - 2{y}^{'}\left(2\right)$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
Given, $y = {x}^{x} \implies \ln \left(y\right) = x\ln \left(x\right)$

Differentiate both sides w.r.t. $x \frac{1}{y}.y' = 1 + \ln \left(x\right) \implies y' = y\left(1 + lnx\right).......(1) \implies y' = {x}^{x}\left(1 + lnx\right)$

at $x = 2 \implies y = 4$

So, $y'(2) = 4\left(1 + ln2\right).......(2)$

Now differentiate the equation $\left(1\right)$,

$y" = y'\left(1 + \ln x\right) + \frac{y}{x} \implies y"(2) = y'\left(1 + \ln 2\right) + 2 \implies y"(2) - y'(2) = y'(\ln 2) + 2 \implies y"(2) - 2y'(2) = \left(\ln 2 - 1\right)y'(2) + 2 = 4(\ln 2 - 1)(\ln 2 + 1) + 2 = 4{\left(\ln 2\right)}^{2} - 2$

,

questions.question: If $2{x}^{y} + 3{y}^{x} = 20,$ then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $\left(2,2\right)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Given,

$2{x}^{y} + 3{y}^{x} = 20$

Now differentiating both sides w.r.t $x,$ we get

$2{x}^{y}\left({y}^{'}\ln x + \frac{y}{x}\right) + 3{y}^{x}\left(\ln y + \frac{x}{y} \cdot {y}^{'}\right) = 0 \left(\text{here }\ln = {\log }_{e}\right)$

Putting $x = 2 & y = 2,$ we get

$\implies 8\left(\ln 2 \cdot {y}^{'} + 1\right) + 12\left(\ln y + {y}^{'}\right) = 0 \implies 8\left(\ln 2 \cdot {y}^{'} + 1\right) + 12\left(\ln y + {y}^{'}\right) = 0 \implies {y}^{'} = - \left(\frac{3\ln 2 + 2}{2\ln 2 + 3}\right) \implies {y}^{'} = - \left(\frac{2 + \ln 8}{3 + \ln 4}\right)$

`

questions.question: If $y\left(x\right) = {\left({x}^{x}\right)}^{x},x > 0$ then $\frac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}} + 20$ at $x = 1$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

$y\left(x\right) = {\left({x}^{x}\right)}^{x}$

Taking ${\log }_{e}$ both side

$\ln y\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} \cdot \ln x$

Now differentiating both side w.r.t $x$ we get,

$\frac{1}{y\left(x\right)} \cdot {y}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{{x}^{2}}{x} + 2x \cdot \ln x {y}^{'}\left(x\right) = y\left(x\right)\left(x + 2x\ln x\right)$ .......(i)

Given $y\left(1\right) = 1$, so ${y}^{'}\left(1\right) = 1$

Now rewriting equation (i) again we get,

$\frac{dx}{dy} = \frac{1}{{x}^{{x}^{2} + 1}\left(1 + 2\ln x\right)}$

Now $\frac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}} = \frac{d}{dx}\left({\left({x}^{{x}^{2} + 1}\left(1 + 2\ln x\right)\right)}^{ - 1}\right)\frac{dx}{dy} \implies \frac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}} = \frac{ - {x}^{{x}^{2}}\left(1 + 2\ln x\right)\left({x}^{2} + 3 + 2{x}^{2}\ln x\right)}{{\left({x}^{{x}^{2}}\left(1 + 2\ln x\right)\right)}^{3}} \times 1 \implies {\left(\frac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}}\right)}_{x = 1} = - 4$

So, ${\left(\frac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}}\right)}_{x = 1} + 20 = - 4 + 20 = 16$

questions.question: If $y(x) = {\cot }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1 + \sin x} + \sqrt{1 - \sin x}}{\sqrt{1 + \sin x} - \sqrt{1 - \sin x}}\right),x \in \left(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi \right)$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = \frac{5\pi }{6}$ is:
questions.explanation:
$y(x) = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\frac{\sqrt{1 + \sin ⁡x} + \sqrt{1−\sin ⁡x}}{\sqrt{1 + \sin ⁡x}−\sqrt{1−\sin ⁡x}}$

As we know that, $\sqrt{1 - \sin ⁡x} = \left(\sin \frac{x}{2} - \cos \frac{x}{2}\right) & \sqrt{1 + \sin ⁡x} = \left(\sin \frac{x}{2} + \cos \frac{x}{2}\right) y(x) = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\frac{\left(\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}\right) + \left(\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2}−\sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}\right)}{\left(\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}\right)−\left(\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2}−\sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}\right)} = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\frac{\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \sin ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}−\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2}}{\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}−\sin ⁡\frac{x}{2} + \cos ⁡\frac{x}{2}}\text{ for }x \in \left(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi \right) = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\left(\frac{\sin ⁡\frac{x}{2}}{\cos ⁡\frac{x}{2}}\right) = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\left(\tan ⁡\frac{x}{2}\right) = {\cot }^{−1}⁡\left(\cot ⁡(\frac{\pi }{2} - \frac{x}{2})\right) y(x) = \frac{\pi }{2}−\frac{x}{2} {y}^{′}(x) = −\frac{1}{2}$

questions.question: Let $f(x) = \cos \left(2{\tan }^{ - 1}\sin \left({\cot }^{ - 1}\sqrt{\frac{1 - x}{x}}\right)\right),0 < x < 1$. Then:
questions.explanation:
Put $x = {\sin }^{2}\theta ,0 < x < 1 \sin \theta = \sqrt{x} \implies f\left(x\right) = \cos \left(2{\tan }^{ - 1}\sin \left({\cot }^{ - 1}\sqrt{\frac{1 - {\sin }^{2}\theta }{{\sin }^{2}\theta }}\right)\right) \implies f\left(x\right) = \cos \left(2{\tan }^{ - 1}(\sin \theta )\right) \implies f\left(x\right) = \cos \left(2{\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{x}\right) = \frac{1 - {\tan }^{2}\left({\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{x}\right)}{1 + {\tan }^{2}\left({\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{x}\right)} \implies f\left(x\right) = \frac{1 - x}{1 + x} \implies {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{\left(1 + x\right)\left( - 1\right) - \left(1 - x\right) \cdot 1}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}} \implies {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{ - 2}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

Multiply, ${\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}$ on both sides

$\implies {\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{ - 2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}}$

Now, $2{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = \frac{2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}} ∴{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) + 2{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = 0$ option $\left(1\right)$ satisfied

;

questions.question: If $f\left(x\right) = \sin \left({\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{1 - {2}^{2x}}{1 + {2}^{2x}}\right)\right)$ and its first derivative with respect to $x$ is $- \frac{b}{a}{\log }_{e}2$ when $x = 1,$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers, then the minimum value of $\left({a}^{2} - {b}^{2}\right)$ is _______.
questions.explanation:
Given $f\left(x\right) = \sin \left({\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{1 - {2}^{2x}}{1 + {2}^{2x}}\right)\right)\text{ at }x = 1;{2}^{2x} = {\left({2}^{x}\right)}^{2}$

For $\sin \left({\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{1 - {\left({2}^{x}\right)}^{2}}{1 + {\left({2}^{x}\right)}^{2}}\right)\right)$

Let ${\tan }^{ - 1}{2}^{x} = \theta ;\theta \in \left( - \frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\right) ∴\sin \left({\cos }^{ - 1}\cos 2\theta \right) = \sin 2\theta \left( \begin{matrix}\text{ If } & x > 1 \implies \frac{\pi }{2} > \theta > \frac{\pi }{4} \\ ∴ & \pi > 2\theta > \frac{\pi }{2}\end{matrix} \right) = 2\sin \theta \cos \theta = \frac{2\tan \theta }{1 + {\tan }^{2}\theta }$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = \frac{2 \cdot {2}^{x}}{1 + {2}^{2x}} ∴{f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{\left(1 + {2}^{2x}\right)\left(2.{2}^{x}\ln 2\right) - {2}^{2x} \cdot 2 \cdot \ln 2 \cdot 2 \cdot {2}^{x}}{\left(1 + {2}^{2x}\right)} ∴{f}^{'}\left(1\right) = \frac{20\ln 2 - 32\ln 2}{25} = - \frac{12}{25}\ln 2$

So, $a = 25,b = 12$.

Then, $\left({a}^{2} - {b}^{2}\right) = {25}^{2} - {12}^{2} = 625 - 144 = 481$

questions.question: If $y(\theta)=\frac{2 \cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta}{\cos 3 \theta+4 \cos 2 \theta+5 \cos \theta+2}$, then at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}, y^{\prime \prime}+y^{\prime}+y$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & y=\frac{2 \cos \theta+2 \cos ^2 \theta-1}{4 \cos ^3 \theta-3 \cos \theta+8 \cos ^2 \theta-4+5 \cos \theta+2} \\ & y=\frac{\left(2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta-1\right)}{\left(2 \cos ^2 \theta+2 \cos \theta-1\right)(2 \cos \theta+2)} \\ & y=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{1+\cos \theta}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=\frac{1}{2} \\ & y^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{-1}{(1+\cos \theta)^2} \times(-\sin \theta)\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} y^{\prime \prime} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\cos \theta(1+\cos \theta)^2-\sin \theta(2)(1+\cos \theta)(-\sin \theta)}{(1+\cos \theta)^4}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \quad y=1\end{aligned}$

questions.question: If ${\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{y}{2}\right) = {\log }_{e}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}^{5},\left(y\right) < 2$, then
questions.explanation:
Given,

${\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{y}{2}\right) = {\log }_{e}{\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)}^{5}$

Using property $\log {x}^{m} = m\log x$ we get,

${\cos }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{y}{2}\right) = 5{\log }_{e}\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)$

Now differentiating both side w.r.t $x$ we get,

$\frac{ - 1}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{{y}^{2}}{4}}} \cdot \frac{{y}^{'}}{2} = 5 \cdot \frac{1}{\frac{x}{5}} \cdot \left(\frac{1}{5}\right) \implies \frac{ - {y}^{'}}{\sqrt{4 - {y}^{2}}} = \frac{5}{x} \implies - x{y}^{'} = 5\sqrt{4 - {y}^{2}}$

Again differentiating w.r.t $x$ we get,

$\implies - x{y}^{''} - {y}^{'} = 5 \cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{4 - {y}^{2}}}\left( - 2y{y}^{'}\right) \implies x{y}^{''} + {y}^{'} = \frac{5yy'}{\sqrt{4 - {y}^{2}}} \implies x{y}^{''} + {y}^{'} = \left(5y\right) \cdot \left( - \frac{5}{x}\right) \implies {x}^{2}{y}^{''} + x{y}^{'} = - 25y \implies {x}^{2}{y}^{''} + x{y}^{'} + 25y = 0$

`

questions.question: Let $f : S \to S$ where $S = \left(0, \infty \right)$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f\left(x + 1\right) = xf\left(x\right)$. If $g : S \to R$ be defined as $g\left(x\right) = {\log }_{e}f\left(x\right)$, then the value of $\left({g}^{''}\left(5\right) - {g}^{''}\left(1\right)\right)$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
$lnf\left(x + 1\right) = ln\left(xf\left(x\right)\right) lnf\left(x + 1\right) = lnx + lnf\left(x\right) \implies g\left(x + 1\right) = lnx + g\left(x\right) \implies g\left(x + 1\right) - g(x) = lnx \implies {g}^{''}\left(x + 1\right) - {g}^{''}\left(x\right) = - \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$

Put $x = 1,2,3,4 {g}^{''}\left(2\right) - {g}^{''}\left(1\right) = - \frac{1}{{1}^{2}}...\left(1\right) {g}^{''}\left(3\right) - {g}^{''}\left(2\right) = - \frac{1}{{2}^{2}}...\left(2\right) {g}^{''}\left(4\right) - {g}^{''}\left(3\right) = - \frac{1}{{3}^{2}}...\left(3\right) {g}^{''}\left(5\right) - {g}^{''}\left(4\right) = - \frac{1}{{4}^{2}}...\left(4\right)$

Add all the equations we get

${g}^{''}\left(5\right) - {g}^{''}\left(1\right) = - \frac{1}{{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{{2}^{2}} - \frac{1}{{3}^{2}} - \frac{1}{{4}^{2}} \left({g}^{"}\left(5\right) - {g}^{"}\left(1\right)\right) = \frac{205}{144}$

questions.question: If ${y}^{1 / 4} + {y}^{ - 1 / 4} = 2x,$ and $\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\frac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} + \alpha x\frac{dy}{dx} + \beta y = 0,$ then $| \alpha - \beta |$ is equal to _______.
Let $y = f\left(x\right) = {\sin }^{3}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\left(\cos \left(\frac{\pi }{3\sqrt{2}}{\left( - 4{x}^{3} + 5{x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)\right)\right)$. Then, at $x = 1$,
questions.explanation:
The given equation can be written as

$y = {\sin }^{3}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\cos g\left(x\right)\right)$

where,

$g\left(x\right) = \frac{\pi }{3\sqrt{2}}{\left( - 4{x}^{3} + 5{x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{3 / 2} \implies {g}^{'}\left(x\right) = \frac{\pi }{2\sqrt{2}}{\left( - 4{x}^{3} + 5{x}^{2} + 1\right)}^{1 / 2}\left( - 12{x}^{2} + 10x\right) \implies {g}^{'}\left(1\right) = \frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}\left( - 2\right) = - \pi$

And,

$g\left(1\right) = \frac{2\pi }{3} = \left(\pi - \frac{\pi }{3}\right)$

Now,

${y}^{'} = 3{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\cos g\left(x\right)\right) \times \cos \left(\frac{\pi }{3}\cos g\left(x\right)\right) \times \frac{\pi }{3}\left( - \sin g\left(x\right)\right){g}^{'}\left(x\right) {y}^{'}\left(1\right) = 3{\sin }^{2}\left( - \frac{\pi }{6}\right) \cdot \cos \left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \cdot \frac{\pi }{3}\left( - \sin \frac{2\pi }{3}\right){g}^{'}\left(1\right) {y}^{'}\left(1\right) = \frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi }{3}\left(\frac{ - \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left( - \pi \right) = \frac{3{\pi }^{2}}{16} y\left(1\right) = {\sin }^{3}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\cos \frac{2\pi }{3}\right) = - \frac{1}{8}$

Therefore,

$2{y}^{'}\left(1\right) + 3{\pi }^{2}y\left(1\right) = 0$

questions.question: Suppose $f\left(x\right) = \frac{\left({2}^{x} + {2}^{ - x}\right)\tan x\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)}}{{\left(7{x}^{2} + 3x + 1\right)}^{3}}$. Then the value of ${f}^{'}\left(0\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \frac{\left({2}^{x} + {2}^{ - x}\right)\tan x\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)}}{{\left(7{x}^{2} + 3x + 1\right)}^{3}}$

We know that, ${f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{f\left(h\right) - f\left(0\right)}{h} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{\frac{\left({2}^{h} + {2}^{ - h}\right)\tan h\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left({h}^{2} - h + 1\right)}}{{\left(7{h}^{2} + 3h + 1\right)}^{3}} - \frac{\left({2}^{0} + {2}^{0}\right)\tan 0\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left(0 - 0 + 1\right)}}{{\left(0 + 0 + 1\right)}^{3}}}{h} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{\left({2}^{h} + {2}^{ - h}\right)\tan h\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left({h}^{2} - h + 1\right)}}{h{\left(7{h}^{2} + 3h + 1\right)}^{3}} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \underset{h \to 0}{\lim }\frac{\left({2}^{h} + {2}^{ - h}\right)\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left({h}^{2} - h + 1\right)}}{{\left(7{h}^{2} + 3h + 1\right)}^{3}} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \frac{\left({2}^{0} + {2}^{0}\right)\sqrt{{\tan }^{ - 1}\left(1\right)}}{{\left(0 + 1\right)}^{3}} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \left(2\right)\sqrt{\frac{\pi }{4}} \implies {f}^{'}\left(0\right) = \sqrt{\pi }$

questions.question: Let $f : R \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{3} + x - 5$. If $g\left(x\right)$ is a function such that $f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = x,∀x \in R$, then ${g}^{'}\left(63\right)$ is equal to ______
questions.explanation:
Here, $g\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = x$ as $f\left(x\right)$ and $g\left(x\right)$ are inverse of each other.

Now, ${g}^{'}\left(f\left(x\right)\right){f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 1 \implies {g}^{'}\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \frac{1}{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)} \dots \left(i\right)$

Now $f\left(x\right) = 63 \implies {x}^{3} + x - 5 = 63 \implies {x}^{3} + x - 68 = 0$

So $x = 4$ satisfies the above equation

${g}^{'}\left(63\right) = \frac{1}{{f}^{'}\left(4\right)}$ from $\left(i\right) = \frac{1}{3{\left(4\right)}^{2} + 1} = \frac{1}{49}$

questions.question: Let $f$ and $g$ be differentiable functions on $R$ such that $fog$ is the identity function. If for some $a,b \in R,{g}^{'}\left(a\right) = 5$ and $g\left(a\right) = b,$ then ${f}^{'}\left(b\right)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
$f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = x \implies {f}^{'}\left(g\left(x\right)\right).{g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 1$

Put $x = a \implies {f}^{'}\left(g\left(a\right)\right){g}^{'}\left(a\right) = 1 \implies {f}^{'}\left(b\right) \times 5 = 1 \implies {f}^{'}\left(b\right) = \frac{1}{5}$

!

questions.question: The derivative of ${\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{2}} - 1}{x}\right)$ with respect to ${\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2x\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}{1 - 2{x}^{2}}\right)$ at $x = \frac{1}{2}$ is :
questions.explanation: Let $x = \tan \theta {y}_{1} = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{\sec \theta - 1}{\tan \theta }\right) = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\tan \frac{\theta }{2}\right) = \frac{\theta }{2} = \frac{1}{2}{\tan }^{ - 1}x x = \sin ϕ,{y}_{2} = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2\sin ϕ\cos ϕ}{\cos 2ϕ}\right) = {\tan }^{ - 1}(\tan 2ϕ) = 2ϕ = 2{\sin }^{ - 1}x \frac{d{y}_{1}}{d{y}_{2}} = \frac{d{y}_{1} / dx}{d{y}_{2} / dx} = \frac{\frac{1}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)} \cdot \frac{1}{2}}{2 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}} = \frac{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}{4\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)} = \frac{\sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{4}}}{4\left(1 + \frac{1}{4}\right)} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}$

questions.question: The derivative of ${tan}^{ - 1}\left(\frac{sinx - cosx}{sinx + cosx}\right)$ with respect to $\frac{x}{2},$ where $x \in \left(0,\frac{\pi }{2}\right)$, is
questions.explanation:
Given function can be written as

$y = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{\sin x - \cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\right) \implies y = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{\tan x - 1}{\tan x + 1}\right) \implies y = {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\tan \left(x - \frac{\pi }{4}\right)\right)\left(\mathrm{given}x \in \left(0,\frac{\pi }{2}\right)\right) \implies y = x - \frac{\pi }{4}$

Now $\frac{dy}{d\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)} = 2\frac{dy}{dx} = 2$
